full_text_en:
**Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Construction Wood Processing General Factory v. China Democratic League Xinjiang Industrial Development General Company — Dispute over House Lease**

**Fa Gong Bu (2002) No. 2**

**Supreme People's Court of the People's Republic of China**

**Civil Judgment**

**(2000) Min Zhong Zi No. 115**

**Appellant (Original Defendant, Counterclaim Plaintiff):** Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Construction Wood Processing General Factory, domiciled at No. 27 Qiantangjiang Road, Urumqi.

**Legal Representative:** Chen Changxing, Chairman of the Board.

**Agent ad litem:** Lü Xianghui, staff member of the Factory.

**Agent ad litem:** Guan Yong, lawyer of Xinjiang Yuanzheng Law Firm.

**Appellant (Original Plaintiff, Counterclaim Defendant):** China Democratic League Xinjiang Industrial Development General Company, domiciled at No. 1 Nanchang Road, Urumqi.

**Legal Representative:** Wang Hongnian, Manager.

**Agent ad litem:** Wu Renhai, Chairman of the Board.

**Agent ad litem:** Wu Ying, lawyer of Xinjiang Fangzhou Law Firm.

Regarding the dispute over house lease between the Appellant Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Construction Wood Processing General Factory (hereinafter referred to as Wood Processing Factory) and the Appellant China Democratic League Xinjiang Industrial Development General Company (hereinafter referred to as Industrial Company), the Appellants appealed against the Civil Judgment (1999) Xin Min Chu Zi No. 13 rendered by the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region. The Supreme People's Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing. Lü Xianghui and Guan Yong, agents ad litem of the Wood Processing Factory, and Wang Hongnian, the legal representative of the Industrial Company, and Wu Renhai and Wu Ying, its agents ad litem, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case has now been concluded.

**Facts Found by the Court**

On October 6, 1992, the Wood Processing Factory and the China Democratic League Xinjiang Urumqi Modern Cultural Exchange Station (hereinafter referred to as the Exchange Station) signed the "Business Building Lease Contract," stipulating that the Exchange Station would lease a four-story business building (including the basement) on the left side of the office building of the Wood Processing Factory, with a construction area of 3,054 square meters, for use as offices, a hotel, a restaurant, a dance hall, etc., for a lease term of 20 years. For the cost of the continued construction of the business building, the Exchange Station was to invest RMB 1,000,000, which should be paid to the Wood Processing Factory as follows: RMB 200,000 within half a month after the contract took effect, RMB 400,000 before the end of March 1993, and the remaining investment amount paid in full before the completion of the project. The RMB 1,000,000 continued construction fee paid by the Exchange Station was to offset the rent; after the offset was completed, rent was to continue to be paid to the Wood Processing Factory according to the contract. The rent was calculated at RMB 20 per square meter per month based on the construction area; payable quarterly in four installments per year, each installment being 25% of the annual rent, with the payment due in the first month of each quarter. The rent price was to remain unchanged for three years after the contract took effect, after which it was to be adjusted separately based on the average market level. Water, heating, and electricity charges were to be paid to the Wood Processing Factory quarterly as stipulated. If the Industrial Company was delinquent in paying rent, a late payment penalty of five-thousandths per day was to be paid. The date on which the business building was formally delivered to the Industrial Company for use was the date from which rent would accrue. The Wood Processing Factory was responsible for handling the lease procedures for the business building. Except for the RMB 1,000,000 invested by the Exchange Station, other costs required for the continued construction of the building were to be borne by the Wood Processing Factory. The design could be made according to the needs of the Exchange Station, provided that the overall structure was not affected. The Wood Processing Factory guaranteed the normal supply of water, heating, and electricity within the leased premises. During the lease term, the Wood Processing Factory was not to interfere with the Exchange Station's right to use and operate the leased premises. Both parties were required to strictly abide by all terms and conditions stipulated in the contract; any party breaching the contract must compensate the other party with liquidated damages equal to 25% of the contract amount and all related economic losses.

On July 26, 1993, the Exchange Station applied to the Urumqi Shaybak District Administration for Industry and Commerce to change its name to the Industrial Company, and the Administration for Industry and Commerce subsequently issued a business license to the Industrial Company with a registered capital of RMB 800,000.

After signing the contract, the Industrial Company paid the Wood Processing Factory RMB 200,000 on November 2, 1992. Further payments were made as follows: RMB 100,000 on May 18, 1993; RMB 400,000 on May 29; RMB 150,000 on June 25; and RMB 300,000 on September 30. The total of the above payments was RMB 1,150,000. Subsequently, from May 1994 to December 1995, the Industrial Company paid the Wood Processing Factory an additional RMB 274,847. Regarding the issue of payments, the judgment of the first instance also found that the disputed business building was originally constructed by the Engineering Team of Shi Xibao under the Great Wall Construction Company, and was later changed to be constructed by Urumqi Tianmei Construction Company (hereinafter referred to as Tianmei Company). Through negotiation among the Industrial Company, the Wood Processing Factory, and Shi Xibao, the Industrial Company paid Shi Xibao RMB 40,000 for the preliminary engineering costs. After receiving the payment, Shi Xibao issued a receipt to the Industrial Company and provided a certificate to the first-instance court. On May 1, 1994, the first to third floors of the business building, constructed by Tianmei Company, were delivered to the Industrial Company, and the basement was delivered to the Industrial Company on January 1, 1995. During construction, the Wood Processing Factory paid a total of RMB 984,081.17 to Tianmei Company for engineering costs, and the remaining amounts were paid by the Industrial Company. In July 1998, the final audited cost of the business building project, as determined by the Industrial Company and the Wood Processing Factory in the "Explanation of the Audit Status of Construction and Installation Works," was RMB 2,235,789.81. The actual amount paid directly by the Industrial Company to Tianmei Company for engineering costs was RMB 1,251,708.64. The total payments made by the Industrial Company to the Wood Processing Factory, Shi Xibao, and Tianmei Company amounted to RMB 2,716,555.64. The Industrial Company actually overpaid RMB 1,716,555.64 for the construction of the business building. Neither party raised any objection to this finding of fact by the first-instance court during the second instance. During the first-instance proceedings, on November 16, 1999, the parties signed two payment lists. The reconciliation conclusion was that the payments made by the Industrial Company to the Wood Processing Factory amounted to RMB 1,424,847, which was undisputed by both parties. The additional payments of RMB 40,000 to Shi Xibao and RMB 10,000 for relocation costs were disputed and were left for the court's determination. The payment of RMB 984,081.17 by the Wood Processing Factory was undisputed by both parties; four other items totaling RMB 95,230 were disputed and were left for the court's determination. On the same day, the parties also signed the "List of Amounts Owed by China Democratic League Xinjiang Industrial Development Co., Ltd. to Xinjiang Construction Wood Processing General Factory," confirming that the Industrial Company owed the Wood Processing Factory RMB 64,005.

Furthermore, in March 1993, the Exchange Station and the Wood Processing Factory signed an "Agreement" stipulating: The Wood Processing Factory agreed to provide a guarantee for the Exchange Station to obtain a bank loan of RMB 1,500,000. The Exchange Station agreed that, upon the availability of the bank loan, it would pay in one lump sum the RMB 800,000 for the continued construction costs stipulated in the lease contract for the business building and simultaneously pay an additional RMB 500,000 as a goodwill deposit. In April 1997, the Urumqi Shaybak District Tax Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the District Tax Bureau) used approximately 325.32 square meters of space on the second floor of the leased premises free of charge as its office. Neither of the two appellants signed a written agreement with the District Tax Bureau permitting the free use of part of the disputed premises. The first-instance judgment found that from January 1, 1996, to May 18, 1999, the Wood Processing Factory subleased two rooms from the Industrial Company, with the annual rent calculated at RMB 18,000 per room, so the Wood Processing Factory owed the Industrial Company rent of RMB 121,500; from March 18, 1997, to February 16, 1998, the Wood Processing Factory subleased another room from the Industrial Company, with the annual rent still at RMB 18,000, so the rent payable was RMB 16,500; from July 17, 1998, to May 18, 1999, the Wood Processing Factory subleased another room from the Industrial Company, with the annual rent still at RMB 18,000, so the rent payable was RMB 15,000. The total rent payable by the Wood Processing Factory for subleasing four rooms from the Industrial Company was RMB 153,000. Neither party raised any objection to the above finding during the second instance.

On June 10, 1997, the Wood Processing Factory and the Industrial Company signed the "Agreement on Collecting Rent for the Golden Triangle," stipulating: Pursuant to the lease contract signed by both parties for the business building, after full consultation, taking into account the clause that the rent would remain unchanged for three years from the effective date of the original contract and would be adjusted separately according to the average market level thereafter, and also considering the actual difficulties of the Industrial Company, it was agreed to calculate rent for the Industrial Company using a preferential plan. That is, the rent receivable for 1996 was 3,054 sqm × RMB 50 × 9 months = RMB 1,374,300; the rent receivable for 1997 was 3,054 sqm × RMB 50 × 12 months = RMB 1,822,400. The rent for 1996 was to be paid in full before the end of July 1997, and the rent for 1997 was to be paid in three installments before the end of December. If payment was not made on time, Clause 7 of the original contract would apply, i.e., default in paying rent would incur a late payment penalty of five-thousandths per day. Regarding the validity of this agreement, the first-instance judgment found that the liquidation group of the Wood Processing Factory did not mention or involve this agreement in its liquidation report submitted to the factory, indicating that the parties had not reached an agreement on the adjustment of rent prices before August 1998. Yu Xinyuan, the head of the liquidation group, confirmed the report's authenticity. The fact that the rent for the four rooms subleased by the Wood Processing Factory from the Industrial Company from 1996 to 1999 was not adjusted also indicated that the parties had not reached an agreement on adjusting the rent price. The Industrial Company argued that the Wood Processing Factory requested the signing of this agreement to cope with superior inspections, that the agreement was false, did not represent the true intentions of the parties, and should be invalid. Yu Xinyuan, head of the liquidation group of the Wood Processing Factory, provided a written "Supplementary Explanation" to the first-instance court stating that the liquidation report reflected only personal views, had not been discussed collectively, did not form a collective opinion of the leadership, and the report text did not bear the official seal of the factory. He argued that the report lacked legal effect and that the first-instance court's use of the report as evidence did not respect objective facts. Employees of the Wood Processing Factory involved in signing the contract provided written testimony to the first-instance court confirming that this agreement was authentic and legal.

It was further found that on June 28, 1998, the parties signed a list of water and electricity charges owed by the Industrial Company to the Wood Processing Factory. The Industrial Company had paid RMB 163,710.5 for water, heating, and electricity charges, owed a total of RMB 441,631.54, and still owed RMB 441,631.54 - RMB 163,710.5 = RMB 277,921.04. In November 1998, the Wood Processing Factory constructed another building adjacent to the disputed premises, with a distance of less than 5 centimeters from the window-side lighting area of the disputed building, affecting the lighting and ventilation of part of the business building site and hindering the normal operation and use of the leased premises. On September 15, 1982, the Wood Processing Factory obtained the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" for its factory site, with the nature of the land being administrative allocation and the purpose being production and living use. The construction of the disputed premises successively obtained project approval documents, construction project planning permits, and construction project construction permits. The General Office of the Autonomous Region People's Government issued a document agreeing that the Wood Processing Factory could establish a comprehensive market commercial city for social services. The Office of the Urumqi Market Construction Leading Group issued a document agreeing that the Industrial Company could open the "Golden Triangle Large Market" and to register with the industry and commerce, fire protection, taxation, and other departments.

It was also found that on January 6, 1997, the Industrial Company issued a power of attorney to Urumqi Xinyuan Commercial Trading Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xinyuan Company, later renamed Urumqi Haikuo Commercial Trading Co., Ltd.), stating: Xinyuan Company would act as an agent for the Industrial Company in collecting rent, water, electricity, and heating fees, property management fees, and loan repayment within the leased building. If the lease contract signed between the agent and the Wood Processing Factory conflicted with the contract signed between the Industrial Company and the Wood Processing Factory, the latter would prevail. The term of agency was from January 6, 1997, to January 5, 2000. Subsequently, the agency term was extended to January 4, 2005. On January 6, 1997, the Wood Processing Factory and Xinyuan Company signed the "Business Building Lease Contract," stipulating: From the date of signing and sealing, the rent would be calculated based on the construction area at RMB 20 per square meter per month, unchanged for three years, and adjusted separately according to the average market level thereafter. On the same day, the parties signed a "Supplementary Contract" stating that if the above agreement conflicted with the "Business Building Lease Contract" signed between the Wood Processing Factory and the Exchange Station on October 6, 1992, the latter agreement would prevail. The Industrial Company used the two agreements signed by the Wood Processing Factory and Xinyuan Company as evidence to deny the content regarding rent increase in the "Agreement on Collecting Rent for the Golden Triangle" signed between the Industrial Company and the Wood Processing Factory.

The Industrial Company filed a lawsuit with the first-instance court, claiming that the Wood Processing Factory had breached the contract, affecting its normal use and operation of the leased premises, and demanded that the Wood Processing Factory bear liquidated damages and compensate for losses and interest. The Wood Processing Factory filed a counterclaim, stating: According to the lease contract, after the RMB 1,000,000 invested by the Industrial Company was offset against the rent, it should continue to pay rent according to the agreement, but in fact, since the building was completed and delivered for use in 1994, the Industrial Company had not paid a single cent of rent. As of August 31, 1998, it had accumulated rent arrears of RMB 6,641,972 and owed water, electricity, and sanitation fees of RMB 331,683.34. During the lease term, the Industrial Company had modified all windows on the first floor of the leased premises into storefronts, posing a serious safety hazard to the building. During the lease term, the Industrial Company conducted obscene performances within the leased premises, which was disclosed by the media, thereby seriously damaging the reputation of the Wood Processing Factory. Accordingly, the Wood Processing Factory requested: The "Business Building Lease Contract" signed by both parties be dissolved; the Industrial Company pay the overdue rent of RMB 6,441,972; pay the water, electricity, heating, and sanitation fees of RMB 331,683.34; pay interest of RMB 57,851.32; pay liquidated damages of RMB 3,579,159.64; restore the floors that were remodelled without authorization to their original condition; issue a public apology in the newspaper to eliminate the adverse impact caused by the obscene performances; and bear all litigation costs.

**Trial of First Instance**

The first-instance court held that the "Business Building Lease Contract" signed by the parties was a valid contract. After signing the contract, the Industrial Company, having already invested RMB 1,000,000 as agreed, made additional investments to pay for the entire construction cost of the business building and completed the building. The Wood Processing Factory failed to fulfill its obligation to make supplementary investments of over RMB 1,000,000 as agreed, which constituted a breach of contract. The Wood Processing Factory's provision of a loan guarantee for the Industrial Company and the house lease relationship between the Wood Processing Factory and the Industrial Company were two different legal relationships. The Wood Processing Factory's argument that changing the investment method did not constitute a breach was untenable. In December 1998, the Wood Processing Factory constructed another building adjacent to the business building leased by the Industrial Company, causing 600 square meters of the business building to lose natural lighting. This severely affected the normal use of the business building by the Industrial Company, causing significant economic losses, and also violated the contract terms, constituting a breach of contract. The economic losses caused to the Industrial Company by the Wood Processing Factory's breach could be compensated by the payment of liquidated damages. The Industrial Company's request for compensation for economic losses was not supported. The losses caused by the District Tax Bureau's free use of 325.32 square meters of the business building could be the subject of a separate claim by the Industrial Company against the District Tax Bureau. The overpayment of RMB 1,716,555.64 by the Industrial Company in constructing the business building should accrue interest from May 1, 1994, the date the Wood Processing Factory delivered the premises, and should be calculated using the method of decreasing principal as it offsets the rent. The rent payable by the Industrial Company to the Wood Processing Factory, totaling RMB 3,445,274.4, when offset against the payments already made by the Industrial Company (RMB 2,716,555.64) and the interest on the overpayment of RMB 1,716,555.64, would basically balance out. The Industrial Company did not delay in paying rent. Therefore, the Wood Processing Factory's counterclaim for late payment penalties and dissolution of the contract was not supported by the first-instance court. The overdue water, electricity, and heating charges of RMB 277,921.04 owed by the Industrial Company to the Wood Processing Factory should be paid, along with late payment interest of RMB 56,511.28. The loan of RMB 64,005 owed by the Industrial Company to the Wood Processing Factory should also be paid. The modifications made by the Industrial Company to the first-floor windows for operational needs during the use of the business building complied with the contract requirements. The Wood Processing Factory's claim that the Industrial Company breached the contract on this basis and demanded restoration to the original condition was not supported by the first-instance court. Accordingly, the court rendered the following judgment:

1.  The "Business Building Lease Contract" signed between the Wood Processing Factory and the Industrial Company is valid.
2.  The Industrial Company's investment of RMB 2,716,555.64 (prepaid rent) plus interest of RMB 731,428 on the Industrial Company's over-investment of RMB 1,716,555.64 totals RMB 3,447,984. As of August 31, 1999, the rent payable by the Industrial Company to the Wood Processing Factory was RMB 3,445,274.4. After offsetting these two amounts, the remaining balance of RMB 2,709.6 is to be used for further rent deduction.
3.  The Wood Processing Factory shall pay the Industrial Company liquidated damages of RMB 3,664,800.
4.  The Industrial Company shall pay the Wood Processing Factory water, electricity, and heating charges of RMB 277,921.04 and late payment interest of RMB 56,511.28.
5.  The Industrial Company shall repay the debt of RMB 64,005 to the Wood Processing Factory.
6.  All other claims of the Industrial Company are dismissed.
7.  All other counterclaims of the Wood Processing Factory are dismissed.

The litigation costs for the main action were RMB 60,210.4, with the Industrial Company bearing 30% (RMB 18,063.12) and the Wood Processing Factory bearing 70% (RMB 42,147.28). The litigation costs for the counterclaim were RMB 58,076.33, with the Industrial Company bearing 40% (RMB 23,230.53) and the Wood Processing Factory bearing 60% (RMB 34,845.80).

The interest of RMB 731,428 in Item 2 of the main text of the first-instance judgment was calculated as follows: When the Wood Processing Factory delivered the rented first to third floors on May 1, 1994, the Industrial Company's overpaid funds of RMB 1,716,555.64 had all been invested in the construction of the rented building. From May 1, 1994, to November 30, 1995, when the RMB 1,000,000 rent offset was completed, interest on the overpaid funds of RMB 1,716,555.64 was calculated without segmentation, at the then-average interest rate of 13.95% per annum, totaling RMB 431,027. After November 30, 1995, rent of RMB 179,430 was deducted each quarter. The principal decreased, and interest was calculated accordingly, totaling RMB 300,401 when the principal was fully offset. The total of these two interest amounts was RMB 731,428.

The liquidated damages of RMB 3,664,800 in Item 3 of the main text of the first-instance judgment were calculated as follows: 20 yuan (monthly rent per square meter) × 3,054 square meters (total area leased by the Industrial Company) × 12 months × 0.25 (liquidated damages rate) × 20 years (contract term) = RMB 3,664,800.

Both the Timber General Factory and the Industrial Company were dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment and appealed to this Court. The Timber General Factory requested on appeal: to overturn the first-instance judgment, find the Industrial Company liable for breach of contract, and order compensation for the economic losses caused to it by the breach. The facts and reasons are as follows: The first-instance judgment lacked factual and legal basis in finding the Timber General Factory in breach. The Industrial Company's failure to pay the rent within the time stipulated in the contract already constituted a breach. The Industrial Company obtained a bank loan to pay the rent, and the Timber General Factory provided a guarantee for the loan. Both parties thus changed the payment method agreed upon in the contract, and it cannot be determined that the Timber General Factory's insufficient payment of the continuation construction funds constituted a breach. According to the contract, the rent for the first three years was RMB 20 per square meter per month; after three years, the parties were to negotiate the price based on the market rate. The first-instance judgment used this price as the rent standard for the period after three years, which violated the contract and infringed upon the Timber General Factory's rights and interests. The "Agreement on the Collection and Payment of Rent for the Golden Triangle" should be deemed valid. The first-instance judgment offset the Industrial Company's excess investment in the continuation construction of the leased premises as rent, and also calculated interest, which violated financial principles; furthermore, it was unknown how the amount of interest was calculated. The first-instance judgment ordering the Timber General Factory to assume liquidated damages of RMB 3,664,800 neither complied with the contract nor had any legal basis, and again it was unknown how this amount was calculated. The first-instance judgment's finding that the Industrial Company's renovation of the leased premises did not constitute a breach was inconsistent with the contract and violated the principle of party autonomy. The first-instance judgment's dismissal of the Timber General Factory's counterclaim lacked factual and legal basis, and the Timber General Factory requested the appellate court to uphold its counterclaim. The Industrial Company was also dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment and appealed to this Court, requesting: to modify the judgment to order the Timber General Factory to compensate the Industrial Company for economic losses of RMB 3,877,894.08 caused by its breach; and to modify the judgment to order the Timber General Factory to compensate the Industrial Company for interest of RMB 2,497,386.74 due to its breach. The facts and reasons are: The Timber General Factory's multiple breaches caused huge economic losses to the Industrial Company. According to Article 31 of the Economic Contract Law: "Where one party breaches an economic contract, it shall pay liquidated damages to the other party. If the losses caused by the breach to the other party exceed the amount of liquidated damages, the breaching party shall also compensate for the shortfall." According to the law, the calculation of interest should be based on the bank's interest rate for the same period. The bank's interest rates for the same period were monthly rates of 16.5%, 15%, 13.725%, and 12.24%, with an average rate of 13.9%. Using this standard, the amount of interest the Timber General Factory should pay to the Industrial Company is RMB 2,222,076.3, not the RMB 731,428 in interest determined by the first-instance judgment.

This Court holds that the "Business Building Lease Contract" signed between the Timber General Factory and the Exchange Station represents the true and voluntary mutual intent of the parties. The nature of the land on which the leased premises are situated is state-owned allocated land. Article 55 of the Urban Real Estate Administration Law provides that where an owner rents out a building constructed on state-owned land for which the right to use was obtained through allocation, the owner shall turn over to the state the land use income component included in the rent. Since the lessor can only collect rent and turn over the land use income component to the state after the lease contract is concluded and takes effect, the payment of land use income is not a precondition for the contract to be concluded and take effect. The Timber General Factory should, in accordance with the law, turn over the land use income component included in the rent collected to the state, register the lease for the record, and obtain a lease permit. The Industrial Company's leasing of the disputed premises to operate the Golden Triangle Market was approved by the relevant departments of the Urumqi Municipal People's Government, and it completed business, tax, and fire safety approval procedures. Accordingly, the first-instance judgment's finding that the "Business Building Lease Contract" was valid is correct and should be upheld. Regarding the validity of the "Agreement on the Collection and Payment of Rent for the Golden Triangle": The "Business Building Lease Contract" stipulated that the rent price of RMB 20 per square meter per month calculated on the basis of gross floor area would remain unchanged for three years after the contract took effect, after which it would be adjusted separately at the market average level. The content of the "Agreement on the Collection and Payment of Rent for the Golden Triangle" is consistent and connected with the main contract's provisions on adjusting the rent standard after three years, and it is a supplementary agreement to the lease contract. The internal liquidation report of the Timber General Factory was unsigned, unstamped, and not discussed by the factory leadership. It was an internal document of the Timber General Factory and had no evidentiary effect externally. The Industrial Company's use of this report as evidence to claim that the agreement was not concluded or was invalid is unfounded. The Timber General Factory's sublease of four rooms to the Industrial Company and the Industrial Company's lease of the Business Building from the Timber General Factory are two separate legal relationships without a necessary causal connection. The Industrial Company's appeal argument that the validity of the "Agreement on the Collection and Payment of Rent for the Golden Triangle" is denied by the fact that the rent for the subleased rooms was not increased also lacks factual and legal basis. On January 6, 1997, the Timber General Factory signed the "Business Building Lease Contract" and the "Supplementary Contract" with Xinyuan Company. Looking at the content of the "Supplementary Contract", it stipulated that if the lease contract signed on January 6, 1997 conflicted with the lease contract signed on October 6, 1992, the lease contract of October 6, 1992 should prevail. The later lease contract stipulated a rent of RMB 20 per square meter per month based on gross floor area, unchanged for three years from the effective date of the contract, and the contract would take effect upon signature and seal by both parties. The earlier lease contract stipulated that the date of formal delivery of the Business Building for use was the rent commencement date. The rent commencement dates stipulated in the two contracts conflicted, so the earlier stipulation should prevail. The Industrial Company's argument that the validity or invalidity of the "Agreement on the Collection and Payment of Rent for the Golden Triangle" is proven by the fact that the rent standards in the two contracts were the same is also unreasonable, because the rent commencement date stipulated in the later contract was invalid and thus lacked probative force. The "Agreement on the Collection and Payment of Rent for the Golden Triangle" bore the seal of the Exchange Station and the signature of Wu Renhai, Chairman of the Industrial Company. The Industrial Company failed to provide evidence that there were circumstances rendering the expression of intent involuntary or unfree at the time of signing the agreement. Therefore, the "Agreement on the Collection and Payment of Rent for the Golden Triangle" should be deemed valid. According to the rent standards stipulated in the "Business Building Lease Contract" and the "Agreement on the Collection and Payment of Rent for the Golden Triangle", the RMB 1,000,000 invested by the Industrial Company was offset as rent until September 12, 1995, and the RMB 1,716,555.64 was offset as rent until April 8, 1997. The Timber General Factory did not raise clear and specific claims regarding whether the Industrial Company had breached the "Agreement on the Collection and Payment of Rent for the Golden Triangle" and how it should bear liability for breach. This Court will not hear issues of breach relating to the performance of this agreement. In March 1993, the "Agreement" signed between the Timber General Factory and the Exchange Station linked the Timber General Factory's guarantee for the Industrial Company's loan to the Industrial Company's advance payment of RMB 800,000 to the Timber General Factory, but did not specify the time for the advance payment. Referring to Article 78 of the Economic Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, where the content of a contract modification agreed upon by the parties is unclear, it is presumed that no modification has occurred. Accordingly, it should be presumed that the method of performance under the original contract was not modified by the signing of this agreement. The other contracts signed by the Timber General Factory to provide guarantees for the Industrial Company's bank loans are independent legal relationships separate from the house lease dispute in this case, and the parties to those contracts are also different from those in this case. The Timber General Factory's appeal argument that the signing of the loan guarantee contract changed the method of performance under the "Business Building Lease Contract" and thus the Timber General Factory should be exempted from liability for breach for not paying the continuation construction investment is unfounded, and this Court does not support it.

According to the stipulations of the "Business Building Lease Contract", the Industrial Company should have paid the RMB 200,000 continuation construction investment for the leased premises before October 21, 1993; it actually paid it in full on November 2, 1993. It should have paid RMB 400,000 before the end of March 1993; it actually paid RMB 100,000 on May 18 and RMB 300,000 on May 29. Its delay in payment constituted a breach. The clause in the contract concerning a late payment penalty of 5 per thousand per day for overdue rent is, in legal nature, a specific liquidated damages clause, effective only for overdue rent. The Industrial Company should bear liability for breach based on this standard. The Timber General Factory's failure to pay the continuation construction investment for the Business Building as stipulated in the contract constituted a breach and should bear liability for breach and compensate the Industrial Company for the losses caused thereby. The interest generated by the Industrial Company's excess investment should be regarded as losses caused to it by the Timber General Factory's breach, to be compensated by the Timber General Factory. The first-instance judgment had two defects in calculating interest, which should be corrected. First, the first-instance judgment's use of an annual interest rate of 13.95% as the interest calculation rate was clearly higher than the highest category of interest rate for the same period stipulated by the state (i.e., the fixed asset loan interest rate), thus violating the principle of legally prescribed interest rates under the Law of the People's Republic of China on the People's Bank of China. The interest should be calculated at the fixed asset loan interest rate for the same period. Second, the first-instance judgment used the period during which the Industrial Company's excess investment was offset as rent as the interest calculation period, without considering the fact that the rent was increased after the "Agreement on the Collection and Payment of Rent for the Golden Triangle" took effect. The Industrial Company's delay in paying the water, electricity, and heating fees owed to the Timber General Factory constituted a breach and it should bear liability for breach. The first-instance judgment ordering it to bear interest for delayed payment without imposing liability for breach lacked legal basis and should be corrected. The "Business Building Lease Contract" stipulated: "Any party that breaches the terms of the contract must pay the other party liquidated damages equal to 25% of the contract amount." That is, if either party breaches, it shall pay liquidated damages to the other party proportionally. Since both parties in this case breached, and the liquidated damages percentages are the same, they offset each other. The Timber General Factory's appeal argument that the Industrial Company unilaterally changed the structure of the premises and engaged in pornographic performances during the lease period is not established due to insufficient evidence, and this Court does not find it. Regarding whether the lessor or the lessee consented to the tax bureau of Shayibake District using 325.32 square meters of the Business Building free of charge, both parties gave inconsistent accounts, and it is difficult to ascertain because neither party nor either party signed a written agreement with the tax bureau. Based on the principle of fairness, the rent standard stipulated in the contract and ordered by the court shall be shared at a ratio of 50%. The Timber General Factory's construction of a building close to the Industrial Company's leased Business Building, which affected the lighting and ventilation of the Industrial Company's leased premises and caused losses to its normal operations, constitutes both a breach of contract and a tort of infringement on neighboring rights. Referring to Article 122 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China: "Where a party's breach of contract infringes upon the personal or property rights of the other party, the injured party has the right to choose to require the breaching party to bear liability for breach under this Law or to bear liability for tort under other laws." The Industrial Company has chosen to pursue the Timber General Factory's liability for breach of contract. There is a lack of quantitative evidence as to whether the losses caused to the Industrial Company by this breach exceed the liquidated damages and whether compensation should be made for the excess. This Court has difficulty making a determination on whether compensation is due or the amount thereof. Since this fact is relatively independent, the right holder may file a separate lawsuit on this matter.

The "Agreement on the Collection and Payment of Rent for the Golden Triangle" only stipulated the rent standard for the period from April 1, 1996, to the end of 1997, and did not stipulate the rent standard for after January 1, 1998. During the performance of the contract, and even during the litigation, the parties could not reach a consensus on the rent standard through negotiation, making the lease contract difficult to continue. The Timber General Factory's request to rescind the "Business Building Lease Contract" is granted by this Court. This Court, based on the stipulations of the "Business Building Lease Contract" and the "Agreement on the Collection and Payment of Rent for the Golden Triangle", the local market conditions for house leasing, the early termination of the lease relationship between the parties, the Industrial Company's investment in constructing the disputed premises, and the appeal requests made by the parties, determines the rent standard for the period from January 1, 1998, until the date of termination of the lease contract as RMB 30 per square meter of gross floor area per month. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Items 1, 5, and 6 of the Civil Judgment (1999) Xin Min Chu Zi No. 13 of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region are affirmed.

2. Items 2, 3, and 7 of the Civil Judgment (1999) Xin Min Chu Zi No. 13 of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region are vacated.

3. The "Business Building Lease Contract" signed between the Timber General Factory and the Industrial Company is rescinded. The Industrial Company shall return the leased premises to the Timber General Factory within 90 days after this judgment takes effect.

4. Within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, the Industrial Company shall pay to the Timber General Factory rent for the period from April 9, 1997, to December 30, 1997 (of which, for 2,728.68 square meters, rent is calculated at RMB 50 per square meter of gross floor area per month; for 325.32 square meters, rent is calculated at RMB 25 per square meter of gross floor area per month).

5. Within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, the Industrial Company shall pay to the Timber General Factory rent for the period from January 1, 1998, to the effective date of this judgment (of which, for 2,728.68 square meters, rent is calculated at RMB 30 per square meter of gross floor area per month; for 325.32 square meters, rent is calculated at RMB 15 per square meter of gross floor area per month).

6. Within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, the Timber General Factory shall pay to the Industrial Company interest on RMB 1,716,555.64 (calculated from September 13, 1995, to April 8, 1997, at the fixed asset loan interest rate for the same period as published by the People's Bank of China).

7. Within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, the Industrial Company shall pay to the Timber General Factory liquidated damages of RMB 123,500 for delayed payment of rent.

8. Item 4 of the Civil Judgment (1999) Xin Min Chu Zi No. 13 of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region is modified as follows: Within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, the Industrial Company shall pay to the Timber General Factory water, electricity, and heating fees of RMB 277,921.04.

9. The other appeal requests of the appellants are dismissed.

The first-instance acceptance fee shall be executed in accordance with the first-instance judgment. The second-instance acceptance fee of RMB 118,286.73 shall be borne by the Industrial Company in the amount of RMB 82,800.71 and by the Timber General Factory in the amount of RMB 35,486.02.

This judgment is final.
